Class TomlResourceBundleProvider

java.lang.Object
java.util.spi.AbstractResourceBundleProvider
be.imgn.toml.i18n.TomlResourceBundleProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
ResourceBundleProvider
public abstract class TomlResourceBundleProvider extends AbstractResourceBundleProvider
Provides TomlResourceBundles to a named module, which cannot load them with TomlResourceBundle.control().

The module declares the service of its bundles, and a provider of it that extends this class. The service is named after the base name of the bundles, as ResourceBundle.getBundle(String, Locale) requires: the bundles com.example.Messages are provided by com.example.spi.MessagesProvider. 

module com.example {
    requires be.imgn.toml;
    uses com.example.spi.MessagesProvider;
    provides com.example.spi.MessagesProvider with com.example.internal.TomlMessagesProvider;
}

public interface MessagesProvider extends ResourceBundleProvider {}

public final class TomlMessagesProvider extends TomlResourceBundleProvider implements MessagesProvider {
    public TomlMessagesProvider() {
        super(TomlMessagesProvider.class.getModule()::getResourceAsStream);
    }
}

ResourceBundle messages = ResourceBundle.getBundle("com.example.Messages", locale);

The provider reads the resources through the opener it is given, because a module encapsulates the resources of its packages: be.imgn.toml cannot read com/example/Messages_fr_BE.toml, but a method reference created in the module com.example can.
